reasoning_traces.think:
The two primitives quantify different aspects of running back performance and route effectiveness. RYOE measures the efficiency of rushing plays relative to expected outcomes based on separation and proximity, while Stacked Box Percentage measures the frequency of contested catches. Together, they form a dual diagnostic: low RYOE indicates poor run-blocking efficiency, while high Stacked Box Percentage indicates poor pass-catching environment. This combination creates a robust "Attrition Edge" signal because injuries to defenders (David Martin-Robinson, Amani Hooker, etc.) degrade both blocking fronts and coverage integrity, simultaneously increasing stacked boxes and reducing rushing efficiency. The mathematical duality lies in their shared dependence on biophysical availability and cognitive load: injured defenders cannot maintain optimal separation distances, leading to both increased contested catches and reduced blocking effectiveness. Failure occurs when injuries affect only one aspect (e.g., cornerbacks get hurt but linemen stay healthy), causing misalignment between the two metrics.
